articles.title: Indiana's mascot starts the season with an absolute heater that puts other mascots to shame
articles.summary: The Indiana Hoosiers mascot Hoosier the Bison zip-lined into Memorial Stadium, then drove an IndyCar around the field during the pregame spectacle.
articles.body: The Indiana Hoosiers began their quest to build on a magical 2025 season that ended with a national championship. It remains to be seen how the year will turn out, but one thing is already certain: their mascot, Hoosier the Bison, will be bringing it every single weekend. The Hoosiers reintroduced a bison mascot for the first time in sixty years last season, and the timing proved to be perfect. MINOR LEAGUE PLAYER GETS SMOKED BY A SCOOTER-RIDING MASCOT IN WILD MOMENT CAUGHT ON CAMERA For his debut, Hoosier skydived into Memorial Stadium. Ripping a speed star like Keanu and Patrick Swayze in "Point Break" is tough to beat for a mascot debut. It was easily the best since Gritty threatened to kill the Penguins mascot. So, for his sophomore season, Hoosier went with the zip line. Not bad, not bad at all. But if that was the extent of the mascottery, it left a little on the table. ...Wait, what's that? I'm being told he also drove around the field in an IndyCar while the marching band performed. Are you not entertained?! HERE'S WHY, EVEN WITH ALL ITS PROBLEMS, COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS STILL BETTER THAN THE NFL That's one of those "The European mind can't comprehend it" moments. "Why is that cow driving a racecar on the pitch while the band is playing?" First of all, it's a "bison" and a "field," and secondly, it's because it's college football, Üter. What a start. I love to see restraint like that on display. Hoosier didn't have to knock everyone's proverbial socks off with the zip line because he knew that there was an open-wheel race car waiting in the wings. You don't see that out of these modern mascots; usually only the blue bloods have the experience to know that you don't want to give away everything with your opener. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fortunately, mascots aren't getting poached by way of NIL (not yet, but give it time) because after that performance, there's no doubt some schools with big checkbooks would be circling him like sharks around fresh chum.

articles.title: El sello de Pedro Martínez se va dejando ver en el Real Madrid: paliza al Baskonia por 121-80
articles.standfirst: Los blancos, con un ritmo vertiginoso y un gran Campazzo, pasan por encima de conjunto vitoriano, muy castigado por las ausencias
articles.summary: Los blancos, con un ritmo vertiginoso y un gran Campazzo, pasan por encima de conjunto vitoriano, muy castigado por las ausencias
articles.body: En el segundo partido de pretemporada, el Real Madrid ya demostró ir pillando la filosofía de Pedro Martínez: el juego vertiginoso, el lanzar el juego desde el rebote defensivo, las posesiones cortísimas... Características del baloncesto que ha implantado el técnico en sus últimos equipos y que va calando en su nueva etapa como madridista. Los suyos las pusieron en práctica ante un Kosner Baskonia muy castigado por las bajas que fue incapaz de oponer resistencia en el primer Memorial Urbano González. Los blancos arrasaron por un contundente 121-80. Resultado consecuencia de que, en plena pretemporada, se juntaran dos situaciones opuestas. El Madrid va cogiendo ritmo con la incorporación de sus jugadores internacionales tras disputar las Ventanas FIBA. Volvieron Feliz y Campazzo, se estrenaron los fichajes Luwawu-Cabarrot, Shulga, Jantunen, Pradilla y también Jones. Los descartes fueron Tavares, al que hay que cuidar tras su lesión del curso pasado, Ndiaye, Procida y Deck, que llegó tocado de un hombro tras jugar con Argentina. El Baskonia, sin apenas rodaje por culpa de los numerosos problemas físicos, y aún con incorporaciones por hacer, está muy lejos aún de ser un equipo. Se dejó notar. La diferencia quedó clara desde un primer cuarto en el que el Madrid se disparó hasta los ¡46 puntos! En esa primera pausa ya ganaba por 20, había repartido 14 asistencias y todos sus jugadores habían anotado, otra característica, el juego coral, muy del nuevo técnico. El encuentro pasó de ser un amistoso a un entrenamiento con aficionados en la grada. Al descanso, ya 78-39. Casi al final del tercer cuarto, +50 con el 106-56. Campazzo, sobre el que hay dudas de su encaje con el baloncesto de Pedro Martínez, fue el mejor. Dirigió y anotó sin apenas errores: 25 puntos con 7/8 en triples y seis asistencias para 32 de valoración. El base conectó con Jones y Sarr en las continuaciones. Se pueden poner las botas haciendo alley-oops. También intimidaron, aunque el primero se cargó de faltas. Shulga, en su regreso a León, donde creció, también tuvo momentos para lucirse. Sufrió en alguna defensa, pero hizo 15 puntos, cinco asistencias y cuatro robos para acabar con 24 de valoración. Buen manejador y creador. También destacaron otros dos pequeños: Maledon y Feliz, con 14 puntos por cabeza. Y Luwawu-Cabarrot (12) dejó pinceladas ofensivas al final del tercer cuarto, cuando los blancos alcanzaron ya los 100 puntos. El Baskonia, ante la relación de su rival, sólo pudo maquillar mínimamente llevándose el último cuarto con el acierto de Spagnolo, que hizo tres puntos en ese periodo para llegar a los 19 puntos. Les queda mucho por construir mientras el Madrid va aprendiendo a volar. 121-Real Madrid (46+32+28+15): Campazzo (22), Shulga (14), Abalde (11), Okeke (5), Sarr (11); Luwawu-Cabarrot (15), Jantunen (6), Feliz (13), Maledon (14), Pradilla (2), Jones (4), Llull (4). 80- Kosner Baskonia (26+13+20+21): Lawson (13), Simmons (7), Duarte (8), Frisch (5), Alves (3); Baugh (6), N'Guessan (12), Spagnolo (19), Souza (-), Ngounoma (7), Alonso (-). Árbitros: Palanca, Carrol y Carpallo. Incidencias: Encuentro correspondiente al I Memorial Urbano González Escapa disputado en el palacio municipal del mismo nombre en León con 5.000 espectadores.

articles.title: Jalen Brunson Responds to Rumor About Former Villanova Teammate Handling Knick Players' Finances
articles.summary: New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson provided some clarity regarding his financial involvement with an old college teammate on Saturday.
articles.body:
New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson provided some clarity regarding his financial involvement with an old college teammate on Saturday.

Brunson responded to a rumor that himself, Josh Hart and Mikal Bridges had become Goldman Sachs Private Wealth Management clients to reunite with former Villanova teammate Matt Kennedy as their financial advisor on social media.

"Matt is my guy but I need your sources," Brunson wrote in a post on X.

Kennedy previously played basketball at Villanova for two seasons from 2016-18, spending time as teammates with Brunson, Hart and Bridges.

He also won a national championship alongside Brunson and Bridges in 2018.

Since Brunson became a member of the Knicks during the 2022 offseason, he's played with several former Wildcats teammates including Hart, Bridges, Donte DiVincenzo and Ryan Arcidiacono.

While DiVincenzo and Arcidiacono weren't members of last season's roster, the other Villanova alumni played key roles during New York's championship run.

Hart showcased his all-around impact in the playoffs by averaging 10.4 points, 8.9 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 1.7 steals per game as Bridges recorded 13.5 points per game on 55.9/36.5/92.0 shooting splits.

Brunson led the NBA in playoff scoring by averaging 28.4 points per game, winning Eastern Conference Finals MVP before taking home Finals MVP honors after the Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs in five games.

articles.title: “I still regret giving him my name”: LeBron James opens up about the pressure his children face as he reflects on fatherhood
articles.summary: NBA News: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ star player, might be an NBA legend but at home, he has been a dedicated and a protective father to his t.
articles.body: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ star player, might be an NBA legend but at home, he has been a dedicated and a protective father to his three children. While there has been a lot of negative speculation about his oldest son, Bronny James, LeBron James has always defended him.LeBron James reflects on the pressure his children face as he opens up about fatherhoodA few years ago, in an episode of The Shop, the NBA legend said, “I still regret giving [Bronny] my name because of [basketball expectations]”.The former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon added, “When I was younger, I didn’t have a dad. So my whole thing was like, whenever I have a kid, not only is he going to be a junior, I’m gonna do everything that this man didn’t do.”LeBron James’ bond with his three children has also been shaped by the lack of a father figure in his life.For the unversed, LeBron James has actually never met his biological father and he was raised single handedly by his mother.Coming from a modest background in Akron, LeBron James’ mother battled through social stigma and financial hardships to raise the NBA legend.LeBron James opens up about how he handles his three children amid his busy career in the leagueWhile LeBron James' life changed as soon as he was drafted by the Cleveland Cavaliers, he has been pretty particular about how he wants to raise his three children.In an interview with Chris Haynes, LeBron James said, “The best part of fatherhood is seeing your kids in you. The stuff that you used to think you could get away with. The things you thought you were sneaking away with and now you see your kids trying the same thing and I be like, ‘I’ve been there, boy. I know what you’re trying to do. I used to try that. Don’t try to fool me. I know exactly what’s going on.’”The 40 year old NBA icon added, “So that’s a pretty cool thing and also just seeing the different personalities from Zhuri, to Bronny, to Bryce, it’s almost like leading a team. You can’t lead them all the same way. They all have different personalities even though we’re all growing up in the same households; you have to be able to command them differently. That’s a challenge, but it’s pretty cool.”Though both LeBron James and his wife Savannah James became parents when they were just teenagers, they never shied away from their responsibilities.Savannah James has also often spoken about how LeBron James stepped up to be there for her even though he himself was pretty young.Today, both of them have built a beautiful life for themselves as they remain private with their lives.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New NBA Rumors on Ben Simmons' Long-Term Future with Kings After Landing 1-Year Contract
articles.summary: Ben Simmons is making his return to the NBA following a year-long hiatus after agreeing to terms on a one-year, $3.5 million contract with the Sacramento Kings.
articles.body:
Ben Simmons is making his return to the NBA following a year-long hiatus after agreeing to terms on a one-year, $3.5 million contract with the Sacramento Kings.

However, Simmons could stay in town longer than next season if all goes well, per ESPN and Andscape's Marc J. Spears.

"Let's say Ben has a great season, regardless of what the Kings do? That he plays well. I don't know if his sister would want me to share this...but she told me the one that's interesting, that's great about Ben for Sacramento, is that he's a pretty loyal guy," Spears told Sactown Sports' The Carmichael Dave Show with Jason Ross . "And if they gave him the opportunity and he does well, and they want him back, and it's fair, I think he'd wanna stay.

"Another thing he likes about Sacramento is when you play in, he's never played in a—people like to pick on the smaller markets—but sometimes, that's a safer haven, right?"

Per Spears , Simmons took the 2025-26 season off to "rehabilitate lingering back and leg injuries."

Simmons also hit the water during his time away, buying a 50 percent stake in the South Florida Sails angling club.

"I needed to get away, and have some space, and just find myself again," Simmons told Clay Skipper of Men's Health in a lengthy June profile.

However, Simmons checked off all the boxes during the Kings' vetting process, which included a workout, a medical exam and meetings with team brass.

Now he's aboard and will serve as the backup point guard to Darius Acuff Jr., the No. 7 overall pick in the NBA draft. However, he's also expected to play all five positions, per Spears.

Simmons was a three-time All-Star during his four NBA seasons on the court with the Philadelphia 76ers (2017-18 to 2020-2021). However, he's played just 108 games since the end of that 2020-21 campaign as a series of injuries have sidelined him for long stretches of time.

Simmons last played in 2024-25 with the Los Angeles Clippers and Brooklyn Nets, averaging 5.0 points, 5.6 assists and 4.7 rebounds over 22.0 minutes per contest in 51 games (24 starts). However, as Simmons told Skipper, he was dealing with serious issues in that season as well.

"Because Simmons's injury involved nerves, he often had shooting pain in his glute and down his leg," Skipper wrote. "He says he felt so fragile that oftentimes he had to change how he breathed."

"People have no idea," Simmons said. "I couldn't walk around."

Now he's in much better shape and has a great opportunity in Sacramento, where he'll assuredly get ample chances to make an impact on a rebuilding team.

articles.title: Enes Kanter reveals his first step after becoming the WNBA Commissioner
articles.summary: Enes Kanter has been in WNBA headlines for all the controversial reasons this past month. He decided to continue causing frustrations by expressing his inter...
articles.body:
Enes Kanter has been in WNBA headlines for all the controversial reasons this past month.

He decided to continue causing frustrations by expressing his interest in the WNBA Commissioner's role, as current Commissioner Cathy Engelbert is set to retire at the end of the current season.

For a man who was thrown out of a WNBA game just a few weeks ago, to expect such a responsibility does not seem right.

But Kanter has his own reasons to believe why he is ideal for the position.

As soon as Englert announced her retirement, he took to X to post a video expressing his interest in the role.

He was asked about the same in an official interview with Fox, where he also revealed his first plan of order.

Kanter reveals he will bring a dictionary

Kanter has been very vocal about his feelings on the transgender discourse taking place in the WNBA.

This has divided opinion, but Kanter seems to be confident that only biological women should be allowed to play the sport.

"I would actually love to," when asked Kanter if he would want to be WNBA Commissioner. "The first thing I would do is bring a dictionary, and tell the whole taskforce what a woman is."

The reason he got thrown out of the arena as well was because of the T-Shirt he wore in the Chicago Sky vs Indiana Fever game.

His T-shirt read, " WOMAN noun. adult human female." What made things worse was his confrontation with Natasha Cloud, who was clearly not happy with what she saw on Kanter's tee.

Kanter isn't the only NBA player who has commented on the WNBA problems. Royce White was also actively involved in this discourse.

The duo announced that they would be attempting to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft. It is unlikely they will be granted permission, but their pursuit of making the sport safe for women continues.

articles.title: Kevin Durant's trainer points out area of emphasis ahead of 2026-27 season
articles.summary: Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant has been working on his game ahead of the 2026-27 season, his 19th year in the NBA.
articles.body:
Ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season, 18-year NBA veteran Kevin Durant has been working on ways to improve his game. In his first season with Houston last year, the former Texas Longhorn performed as advertised, averaging 26 points, 5.5 rebounds, 4.8 assists, 0.9 blocks and 0.8 steals. However, his trainer, Jamal "Dash" Lovell, still sees some areas that need improving.

"When they throw doubles at him and he's tired or fatigued, we want him to get better at not turning the ball over out of the double team. So it's about making sure that he develops as a passer through the double team. So that was one of the points of emphasis from watching his film. It's about making sure that he continues to develop."

Durant's turnover struggles were evident in his lone postseason matchup against the Lakers, giving the ball away nine times. Unfortunately for Houston, Durant was unable to suit up in the team's five other matchups, as the Rockets suffered a 4-2 series defeat and a first-round exit.

Heading into the 2026-27 season, Houston's acquisition of Marcus Smart and the return of Fred VanVleet should take some ball-handling pressure off of Durant.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama Celebrates Salahdine Parnasse's TKO Win vs. Dan Hooker on Video at UFC Fight Night
articles.summary: San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama was thrilled to see fellow Frenchman Salahdine Parnasse earn a first-round TKO over Dan Hooker in a lightweight matchup at UFC Fight Night on Saturday evening.
articles.body:
San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama was thrilled to see fellow Frenchman Salahdine Parnasse earn a first-round TKO over Dan Hooker in a lightweight matchup at UFC Fight Night on Saturday evening.

The event took place in Paris' Accor Arena, where Wembanyama and his younger brother, Oscar Wembanyama, a professional basketball player who plays for Denain Voltaire Basket in France.

The Parnasse-Hooker match served as the main event and lit up the home crowd.

Parnasse, who earned a Performance of the Night bonus, got the TKO after a devastating kick-and-punch combo near the end of the first round.

The fight served as the 28-year-old Parnasse's first bout in UFC. He's 24-2 lifetime in professional MMA, though, and has his sights set on a major talent, Max Holloway.

Ultimately, Parnasse is a fighter to watch moving forward, and he certainly has a big fan in Wembanyama.

articles.title: Chicago Sky Owner Calls Enes Kanter Freedom Lawsuit ‘Meritless And Frivolous’
articles.summary: Chicago Sky owner Michael Alter called Enes Kanter Freedom’s lawsuit meritless and frivolous, saying he was ejected for his conduct, not his speech.
articles.body:
Chicago Sky owner Michael Alter called the federal lawsuit filed by Enes Kanter Freedom "meritless and frivolous" in a statement the team released Friday, one day after the former NBA center sued over his ejection from a WNBA game at Wintrust Arena.

Freedom filed the suit Thursday in U.S. District Court in Illinois. The complaint names Chicago Women's Basketball Operations, LLC, which operates the Sky, along with the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority, which owns the arena, and the city of Chicago. Freedom alleges his First Amendment rights were violated when security removed him from the Sky's Aug. 23 game against the Indiana Fever and when the team later banned him from the building.

Alter said the statement would be his last public comment on the matter, on the advice of the team's legal counsel, with anything further coming in court.

"Freedom's claim that he was removed from Wintrust Arena due to his speech is false," Alter said. "As his own complaint acknowledges, he wore the shirt in question for multiple hours without any contact with security. Security removed Freedom only after he violated fan code of conduct by rising from his seat, gesturing at a player, and stepping toward the court."

"Freedom was removed for his conduct, not his speech," Alter continued. "We look forward to the truth prevailing in court."

Freedom, 34, sat along the baseline that night in a black shirt reading "WOMAN noun. adult human female." With 1:22 left in the third quarter, Sky guard Natasha Cloud scored inside and the Fever called timeout. Cloud chest-bumped teammate Aicha Coulibaly, then turned and walked toward Freedom. She yelled and pointed at him as she approached. Freedom stood, held his arms out, and stepped onto the court. Security and several Sky players moved between the two.

Freedom stopped near the basket to argue with security on his way out. He spun around holding his shirt out toward the crowd as he walked to the lobby, spoke with a group of police officers, and left the arena. Indiana won the game 113-90.

Two days after the game, Alter announced the ban in a news conference with Chicago reporters. He said Freedom had started engaging Cloud from his seat in an effort to provoke her. Freedom will be allowed back, Alter said, only after proving to the team's satisfaction that he can follow its rules "without being a potential threat." A Sky spokesperson confirmed the ban is indefinite.

Freedom is seeking damages and the lifting of that ban.

"The Defendants combined and conspired, and acted jointly to execute their conspiracy, to discriminate against Plaintiff based on Plaintiff's verbal and demonstrable expression of viewpoint and gender identity when they wrongfully ejected Plaintiff from a recent WNBA game," the complaint reads. "Defendants compounded and exacerbated Plaintiff's injuries when they subsequently banned Plaintiff indefinitely from attendance."

Cloud, 34, did not speak with reporters after the Aug. 23 game. Before the Sky played the New York Liberty on Aug. 29, she called Freedom an "irrelevant person" and said she would talk instead about domestic violence, sexual assault, and food insecurity.

Freedom and Royce White, another former NBA player, declared for the WNBA draft earlier this summer, saying they identify as women. A person familiar with the decision told The Associated Press that neither is eligible. Front Office Sports reported the league has ruled Freedom ineligible for the 2027 draft.

The league's collective bargaining agreement restricts the WNBA to women. It contains no further language on gender identity or sex assigned at birth. No transgender woman has played in the league.

The day after the ejection, Freedom told ABC News that he and Cloud exchanged words after a Sophie Cunningham 3-pointer, and that Cloud started cursing at him before he was thrown out.

"You don't have to agree with my speech but you don't get to silence me for it," Freedom posted on social media Thursday. "I will not be intimidated. I will not be silenced. I will continue to stand for women and defend free speech."

Freedom played 11 NBA seasons and last appeared in a game in 2022.

The Sky return from the World Cup break Sept. 17 at home against the Washington Mystics. Chicago will be without Skylar Diggins, who was ruled out for the rest of the season with a right knee injury.

articles.title: What it meant for Jackson State' WR Nate Rembert to have career night vs former team
articles.summary: Jackson State wide receiver Nate Rembert finished with a career-high 179 yards on four catches against his former team Edward Waters on Sept. 5.
articles.body:
Jackson State football quarterback Jared Lockhart could find no real-life comparison for wide receiver Nate Rembert 's performance in the home opener.

Rembert finished with a career-high 179 yards on four receptions in 66-14 win for JSU (2-0) over Division II Edward Waters (1-1) at Mississippi Veterans Memorial Stadium on Sept. 5. All four receptions went for more than 20 yards, and three were gains of 50-plus yards.

"He's like a video game," Lockhart said of Rembert. "Like NCAA. It's a blessing to have him."

The night was memorable for Rembert for more than just his standout performance. Rembert's NCAA career began at EWU in 2023.

Tiger fans met the new Jackson State football team at Bleed Thee Blue Fall Fan Fest

As a freshman he led EWU in receiving touchdowns and finished second on the team in receiving yards to make the All-SIAC first team. His time at EWU built the foundation for his Jackson State career, which includes two All-SWAC honors.

"It was a blessing to be out here, honestly," Rembert said. "I went there in 2023, my freshman year, and my last year, to be able to play against them, it's just a blessing."

Rembert got eligibility in 2026 from a preliminary injunction in a suit against the NCAA.

Rembert graduated from high school in 2021 but didn't begin NCAA competition until 2023. However, the NCAA argued that the time he didn't play football while attending a community college should count against his eligibility.

The fifth-year player made his extra year count against EWU, leading JSU in receiving yards and completing several highlight-worthy plays. Rembert's long receptions came with their fair share of jukes and speed bursts. Of his 179 yards, 119 were gained after the catch.

One play in the third quarter drew a comparison to Reggie Bush in the postgame press conference. Rembert caught the pass on the left side of the field and reversed course, running backward several yards behind the line of scrimmage before finding a 24-yard gain to get JSU across midfield.

"I just seen a whole bunch of their guys setting the edge," Rembert said. "… Now, I wanted to cut, but I'm like, forget it. I'm just going to make something happen. And then when I almost stumbled, I was like, I can't fall because then I'm going to get cussed out. I'm just glad I got the first down and got some yardage on it and make do what I could make do."

Tia Reid covers Jackson State sports for the Clarion Ledger . Email her at treid@usatodayco.com and follow her on X @tiareid65 .

articles.title: El nuevo Barça ilusiona desde dentro: "La gente lo va a pasar bien este año"
articles.standfirst: Las primeras sensaciones que transmite el vestuario tras la catarsis de su plantilla, con 11 fichajes y un nuevo entrenador, son muy positivas
articles.summary: Las primeras sensaciones que transmite el vestuario tras la catarsis de su plantilla, con 11 fichajes y un nuevo entrenador, son muy positivas
articles.body: El Barcelona está aprovechando su 'stage' de pretemporada en Encamp para poner las primeras piedras de un proyecto profundamente renovado, con 11 jugadores nuevos y un entrenador debutante que sustituye a Xavi Pascual. Y las primeras sensaciones que llegan desde el vestuario tras esta catarsis en toda regla son positivas. Aleksander Sekulic destaca especialmente la actitud de sus jugadores durante estos primeros días. "Están haciendo un gran trabajo y tengo sensaciones fantásticas, pero sólo es el principio y es difícil de decir, pero la respuesta de los jugadores es fantástica". El técnico es consciente de que queda mucho camino por recorrer, pero también percibe una mentalidad que invita al optimismo. "Todo el mundo sabe que tenemos un gran reto por delante. Tenemos un nuevo equipo, con nuevos jugadores, nuevo entrenador y muchas cosas nuevas, pero esto es parte del oficio". Y añade: "Con la mentalidad de los jugadores, de los entrenadores y de todo el mundo implicado en el club, podemos superar todos estos retos de forma positiva". Kevin Punter, nuevo capitán junto a Joel Parra y Darío Brizuela, también transmite ambición. "Creo que lo más importante para nosotros es tener la mentalidad correcta y ser ambiciosos. Tener cosas que demostrar". El estadounidense sabe que el nuevo Barça necesita tiempo para ensamblarse: "Así es cómo se acelera el proceso de aprendizaje, jugando a baloncesto y cinco contra cinco". Y advierte: "Esto llevará tiempo, ya que algunos jugadores tendrán que aprender rápidamente algunas normas". Juan Núñez afronta el curso con la intención de dejar atrás las dificultades de las dos últimas temporadas y recuperar las buenas sensaciones. "Este verano ha servido para borrar las dos últimas temporadas y para tirar hacia adelante". Su objetivo es volver a disfrutar: "Juego para pasármelo bien y quiero recuperar esa sensación". Y también ayudar al equipo: "Mi objetivo individual es sentirme bien físicamente y ayudar al equipo, pudiendo disfrutar y haciendo disfrutar con mi nuevo juego". El base azulgrana, además, percibe una energía especial en el nuevo vestuario. "Aún no llevamos muchos entrenamientos pero la energía del equipo es joven, con un juego rápido, alegre y divertido. La gente se lo pasará bien este año". Un mensaje que resume las primeras sensaciones de un Barça que todavía necesita tiempo, pero que ya transmite ilusión, ambición y ganas de crecer. El calendario obligará a acelerar el proceso, con la Lliga Catalana, la Supercopa y, casi sin margen, los estrenos en Euroliga y ACB. El nuevo proyecto azulgrana ya empieza a ilusionar desde dentro.

articles.title: España, desalojada de su hotel de madrugada
articles.standfirst: Saltó la alarma de incendios pasadas las 2.00 AM y acudieron los bomberos
articles.summary: Saltó la alarma de incendios pasadas las 2.00 AM y acudieron los bomberos
articles.body: La selección española, al igual que el resto de participantes de la Copa del Mundo de Berlín, fueron desalojadas de su hotel de concentración en la madrugada de este domingo tras saltar la alarma de incendios del edificio. "Saltó la alarma de incendios y vinieron los bomberos, pero se marcharon rápido", explicaron a EFE fuentes del combinado nacional de un incidente que no pasó a mayores. Varias jugadoras como la belga Elise Ramette o la australiana Stephanie Talbot, compartieron en su cuenta de Instagram vídeos del momento en el que se ve, pasadas las 02:00 hora local (00.00 GMT), a todas las jugadoras aguardando en la calle junto a la policía. La selección estadounidense fue la única que no se vio afectada por este acontecimiento dado que están alojadas en otro hotel. Este domingo, continúa la disputa de la segunda jornada de la fase de grupos del Mundial con un Italia vs Estados Unidos como plato fuerte del día, además de los duelos entre Turquía vs Australia, China vs Chequia, Puerto Rico vs Bélgica.

articles.title: "Hay superestrellas de la NBA ahora mismo que no podrían jugar en Europa"
articles.standfirst: Un jugador con 12 años de experiencia en la NBA vuelve a encender el debate entre el baloncesto europeo y el estadounidense
articles.summary: Un jugador con 12 años de experiencia en la NBA vuelve a encender el debate entre el baloncesto europeo y el estadounidense
articles.body: El debate sobre las diferencias entre la NBA y el baloncesto europeo vuelve a encenderse con una afirmación contundente de Patrick Beverley. El base estadounidense de 38 años, que jugó 12 años en la NBA (Rockets, Clippers, Wolves, Lakers, Bulls, Sixers y Bucks) y esta temporada lo hará en el Boulazac de la liga francesa, asegura que algunas de las actuales superestrellas de la liga estadounidense no tendrían capacidad para competir en Europa. “Hay superestrellas de la NBA ahora mismo que no podrían jugar en Europa. Lo creo firmemente. Simplemente no podrían”, aseguró en el programa de YouTube Thanalysis, presentado por Thanasis Antetokounmpo, que juega en los Bucks, donde compartía equipo con su hermano, la superestrella Giannis Antetokounmpo, hasta que este fue traspasado hace dos meses a los Miami Heat. La clave, según Beverley, no está tanto en el físico como en la mentalidad y en la capacidad de adaptación a un baloncesto mucho más colectivo. “No es una falta de respeto a la capacidad física de cada uno, sino a la mentalidad”, explicó el veterano jugador, que conoce perfectamente ambos mundos después de haber desarrollado buena parte de su carrera en Europa antes de dar el salto a la NBA en 2013. Beverley pone el acento en un cambio radical de roles. En Europa, sostiene, el equipo está por encima de cualquier individualidad y el entrenador tiene un control mucho mayor sobre el juego. “Todo gira en torno al equipo. El entrenador lo controla todo. Es casi como un equipo universitario formado por adultos. El equipo está por encima de cada individuo”, afirmó. Una filosofía que, a su juicio, podría resultar difícil de asumir para algunas estrellas acostumbradas a tener un protagonismo muy superior en la NBA. También el propio juego exige una adaptación profunda. Beverley recuerda que en Europa se puede jugar una posesión completa sin buscar un lanzamiento hasta los últimos segundos y que “todo se basa en la defensa”. A ello añade aspectos fuera de la pista que considera igualmente determinantes, desde compartir habitación con un compañero hasta afrontar viajes menos cómodos. Una reivindicación del baloncesto europeo desde la voz de alguien que ha vivido los dos mundos y que ahora vuelve a ponerse a prueba en Francia.

articles.title: El último niño mimado de la NBA: otro novato multimillonario
articles.standfirst: El escolta Amen Thompson, rookie de 23 años de los Rockets, acuerda una renovación por cinco años y 208 millones de dólares
articles.summary: El escolta Amen Thompson, rookie de 23 años de los Rockets, acuerda una renovación por cinco años y 208 millones de dólares
articles.body: El dinero sigue cayendo del cielo en la NBA. Amen Thompson se ha convertido en el nuevo novato multimillonario después de acordar con los Houston Rockets una renovación de cinco años y 208 millones de dólares, según adelantó Shams Charania en ESPN. El contrato incluye además una cláusula de bonificación por traspaso del 10% y mantendrá al escolta bajo contrato con Houston hasta 2032. A sus 23 años, Thompson ha justificado semejante apuesta con una progresión meteórica desde que fue elegido en el número 4 del Draft de 2023. La pasada temporada alcanzó máximos de carrera en puntos (18,3), asistencias (5,3) y robos (1,5), lideró la NBA en minutos disputados y terminó entre los mejores de la Liga en robos y recuperaciones de balones. Su impacto va mucho más allá de una posición concreta. La ausencia de Fred VanVleet le llevó a ejercer principalmente como base, pero Thompson tiene capacidad para ocupar cualquiera de las posiciones exteriores e incluso jugar en la pintura. La temporada pasada fue, además, uno de los nueve jugadores que promediaron al menos 18 puntos, siete rebotes y cinco asistencias, compartiendo lista con estrellas como Nikola Jokic, Luka Doncic, Giannis Antetokounmpo y Jayson Tatum. Los Rockets blindan así a toda su joven columna vertebral después de haber renovado también a Alperen Sengun, Jabari Smith Jr. y Tari Eason, mientras Kevin Durant aporta la experiencia de una superestrella. Thompson es, además, el segundo jugador de la camada de 2023 que firma una extensión de novato, tras Victor Wembanyama. Y la lluvia de millones no parece haber terminado: Brandon Miller, Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George, Cason Wallace, Jaime Jaquez Jr. y Brandin Podziemski aparecen entre los candidatos a sellar próximamente sus propios contratos de oro.

articles.title: ‘Pablo (Torre) Looking Into This Right Now’ – NBA World Reacts as Jalen Brunson Clears the Air Over Goldman Sachs-Related Speculation
articles.summary: On Friday, a report linking Jalen Brunson, Josh Hart, and Mikal Bridges to former Villanova teammate Matt Kennedy as part of their financial advisor team wen...
articles.body:
On Friday, a report linking Jalen Brunson, Josh Hart, and Mikal Bridges to former Villanova teammate Matt Kennedy as part of their financial advisor team went viral. The report claimed that the New York Knicks stars had become clients of Goldman Sachs Private Wealth Management through Kennedy.

Brunson addressed the report the following day, questioning the source behind the claim. His response quickly caught the attention of the NBA community, with fans piling into the discussion and bringing their own theories and jokes.

Jalen Brunson's Goldman Sachs Clarification Sparks Reactions Across NBA Community

A Bloomberg report , syndicated by Wealth Management, stated that the Knicks' 2026 championship was "a win for Goldman's massive wealth-management business," which counts some Knicks players among its clients.

According to the report, Kennedy is part of the team handling some of Goldman Sachs' business with Knicks players. Kennedy, though, declined to comment.

On X, Shortsqueez, a self-described "finance newsletter read by 250,000 bankers + investors," claimed Friday that Kennedy had become the financial advisor for Brunson, Hart, and Bridges.

Brunson responded directly to the viral post:

"Matt is my guy, but I need your sources."

The Knicks captain's message only fueled online reactions.

"Pablo (Torre) looking into this right now," one sports fan wrote.

"Boy, you can't run from this investigation. Lol," a n Oklahoma City Thunder supporter added.

"Yo, king of New York, why they lying on your name," a basketball observer commented.

Torre's name surfaced in the reactions because of his reporting on the Los Angeles Clippers' salary-cap circumvention deals involving Kawhi Leonard. The journalist and podcaster, however, had no known involvement in the Brunson-Kennedy report.

Other fans focused less on Brunson's response and more on the financial-advisor angle.

"So much for client confidentiality! That's the hallmark of a professional Financial Advisor," one basketball observer wrote .

"When your financial advisor has actual championship experience," another NBA supporter remarked.

Some fans also speculated about how the report came together.

"They probably just saw you in meetings and connected the dots," an X user suggested.

Goldman Sachs counts several high-profile celebrities, including athletes, among its clients, and Kennedy is part of the company's wealth-management operation. That makes it possible for a business relationship between the Knicks players and Goldman Sachs to form through Kennedy.

Still, the former Dallas Mavericks guard's response made clear that he wanted to know the source behind the specific claim that Kennedy was serving as the trio's financial advisor.

Kennedy played for Villanova during the 2016-17 and 2017-18 seasons, and was part of the Wildcats' supporting cast during Brunson, Hart, and Bridges' time at the school. Hart left for the NBA after the 2016-17 campaign, while Brunson and Bridges remained at Villanova for another championship run.

For Brunson, the viral report was less about the claim itself and more about how the information reached the public. His request for the source added another layer to a story that had already generated plenty of attention online.

images.caption: Jalen Brunson addresses Goldman Sachs-related speculation, sparking reactions from the NBA world and plenty of attention from fans.

articles.title: Ex-College Basketball Player Breaks Down How WNBA Treatment of Caitlin Clark Hurts Olivia Miles’ MVP Chances
articles.summary: The WNBA is on an unusual break due to the 2026 FIBA World Cup, but the MVP debate is showing no signs of slowing down. With only a handful of regular-season...
articles.body:
The WNBA is on an unusual break due to the 2026 FIBA World Cup, but the MVP debate is showing no signs of slowing down. With only a handful of regular-season games remaining once the league resumes, A'ja Wilson remains the frontrunner for the award. However, the conversation behind her has become just as interesting, with Caitlin Clark and Olivia Miles emerging as two of the most debated names in the race. But former Old Dominion college basketball player Rachel DeMita believes the difference in how defenses approach them makes the conversation even more complicated.

A fan recently argued on a Courtside Club YouTube video that while Miles has been excellent, she should not be ranked above Clark or Kelsey Mitchell in the MVP conversation because she does not face the same level of defensive attention. And while DeMita agreed with part of that argument, she also explained why using defensive treatment as an MVP metric can get tricky.

"I think Olivia Miles has been great. She is clear Rookie of the Year this season… The kind of defense that we see on Caitlin Clark from season one – Olivia Miles doesn't experience that sort of defense," DeMita replied on Courtside Club in an X post. "And I actually think that people haven't even been guarding Caitlin Clark this year like they did her rookie season. Full-court pressure, face guarding, all of that kind of stuff. I think she's clear unanimous Rookie of the Year."

"But when you're talking about MVP and other awards like that, it would be really hard if we use that metric of 'Oh, they're not guarded the same.' But it would be hard to use that metric when talking about each player because it is subjective. It's always going to be subjective. It's not just one metric."

"Kelsey Mitchell, for example, has a quicker first step than Caitlin. You don't want to push up on Kelsey, and also Kelsey's smaller." she added. "You kind of want to sit back a little bit, or else she will blow by you. And so I agree with you to a certain extent, especially how we saw Caitlin guarded in her rookie season. How we see teams like just lasered in on her. However, it's hard to use that as a metric to how you decide who should be MVP because it just gets kind of sticky," she further added.

Both Clark and Miles have made strong cases in very different ways. Clark has the individual numbers, while Miles has helped lead the Minnesota Lynx to the best record in the league despite entering the season as a rookie. That has naturally sparked a debate over which guard has been more valuable.

The Lynx entered the season with plenty of uncertainty after Napheesa Collier missed a significant portion of the campaign with an injury. Yet Minnesota has remained at the top of the standings, with Miles playing a major role in keeping the team there.

The rookie is averaging 19.7 points and 6.0 assists per game while helping the Lynx to a 31-9 record heading into the break. She also leads the team in both categories. That production, combined with Minnesota's success, has made her difficult to ignore in the MVP conversation, while many considered her a lock for the ROTY.

But Caitlin Clark has the statistical advantage. The Fever guard is averaging 22.5 points (third-best in the WNBA) and a league-best 8.4 assists per game, although Indiana enters the break in fifth place at 26-14.

That is where the defensive-treatment argument comes back into play. If Clark is regularly drawing more aggressive defensive schemes than Miles, it is fair to consider how much that affects the difficulty of what each player is being asked to do. However, DeMita does not believe that distinction can simply settle the MVP debate.

For Miles, that leaves an interesting situation. Her numbers and Minnesota's record have put her firmly in the conversation, but comparing her directly with Caitlin Clark requires more than looking at statistics or defensive schemes alone. With the WNBA season nearing its final stretch, the debate may ultimately come down to how voters weigh individual production, team success, and the different challenges each star faces every night.

Both guards have made strong cases in very different ways. But for many, including WNBA legend Diana Taurasi, the MVP race still appears to be leaning in the direction of Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson.

articles.title: El padre de Doncic da detalles de la minitemporada de los Lakers en Eslovenia: "Fue inolvidable"
articles.standfirst: Sasa Doncic asegura que la concentración de los angelinos "fue de maravilla"
articles.summary: Sasa Doncic asegura que la concentración de los angelinos "fue de maravilla"
articles.body: La Liga ABA celebró su 25 aniversario, y Sasa Doncic, padre de Luka Doncic, también estuvo presente en la ceremonia celebrada en Ljubljana. El progenitor de la estrella de los Lakers y director deportivo del Ilirija fue uno de los invitados al evento. En una entrevista con Mozzart Sport, el señor Doncic senior habló de la ceremonia, del crecimiento de la Liga ABA y, cómo no, de los Lakers de su hijo, al ser preguntado por la minitemporada de cuatro días que hicieron los angelinos el pasado mes en Eslovenia. Doncic agasajó a sus compañeros durante cuatro días en su país, encargándose de asumir todos los gastos -incluidos avión privado, alojamientos y actividades como jugar al golf o ir de pesca- para hacer equipo de cara a la nueva temporada de la NBA en la que tendrán que suplir la marcha de LeBron James. Sasa Doncic, por lo que le ha contado su hijo, asegura que la reunión fue todo un éxito y muy productiva para hacer equipo: "Estuvieron allí, lo pasaron de maravilla y todo fue muy bien, algo inolvidable, o al menos eso me dijeron a mí. No sé, el tiempo lo dirá. Tengo muchas ganas de ver qué pasa. Por supuesto apoyo a los Lakers por Luka y tengo ganas de ver si Rob Pelinka ha formado un buen equipo, ya veremos", concluyó.

Caitlin Clark recorded a record-setting double-double with 14 points on 4-for-9 shooting from the floor, including 3-for-7 from 3-point distance, and 3-for-4 at the free-throw line, alongside the aforementioned 11 assists and three added rebounds in 25:19 of play.

While the 6-foot guard was not part of the starting lineup against China, her dominant showing earned her both Team USA and TCL Player of the Game recognition.

articles.title: 5 NBA Players Ready To Make The Leap
articles.summary: Predicting a player's leap in the NBA can be extremely difficult, but some young players, based on their play last season, may be on the verge of taking the next step in their development.
articles.body:
Predicting a player's leap in the NBA can be extremely difficult, but some young players, based on their play last season, may be on the verge of taking the next step in their development.

There were several leap stories last season: Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Jalen Duren (ignore his playoff performance), Deni Avdija.

The leap can happen for several reasons, most commonly because more time in the NBA system opens the door. Other cases can come from a change in the situation, whether it's moving to a new team or more opportunities opening up when someone leaves. Sometimes it's finally getting healthy at the right time that gives a player a chance to show what they can do.

Below are a few candidates—some more obvious than others—that are fully capable of taking a huge leap next season.

Second-year players are expected to make a leap after going through their first season. Dylan Harper of the Spurs might be in a different category, as his leap could be bigger than most people are ready for.

Harper came into his rookie year looking more advanced than most rookies. But it largely went unnoticed during the regular season because he was coming off the bench. He only started four games and averaged 22.6 minutes per game, averaging 11.8 points and 3.9 assists and finishing fourth in Rookie of the Year voting. He struggled from three for most of the year, but in the last 21 games, he shot 53.6 percent on 2.7 attempts.

As the playoffs began, Harper's shooting didn't carry over, but he remained a consistent source of good basketball for the Spurs. It didn't matter what defender was in front of him; he could get to the rim at will and finish. And as many of his teammates struggled in the finals, he shined . He was second in scoring for San Antonio, averaging 18 points per game, and his minutes went up to 31 per contest during the series.

This coming season, Harper should receive a larger role from the Spurs despite De'Aaron Fox playing in front of him. Coach Mitch Johnson has the luxury of pairing him with Fox or Stephon Castle—at times, playing all three together.

Harper may still come off the bench, but there are more minutes out there for him, especially if he can become a more consistent shooter like he was at the end of the regular season.

Harper came into his rookie season not playing like a rookie and after the run he had in the Finals, expect him to make a major leap next season that goes beyond just a rookie into his sophomore season.

There's an argument that Ajay Mitchell's leap happened last season. He burst onto the scene for the Thunder, with Jalen Williams dealing with injuries. But Mitchell still has room to grow.

Over the last two seasons, Mitchell has played only 93 games because of the Thunder's depth. That depth has gotten a little thinner with OKC moving off Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe. And all of that means more minutes and opportunities for Mitchell.

Mitchell's minutes went up from 16.6 minutes his rookie season to 25.8 last season. With that minute increase, his points per game shot up from 6.5 to 13.6. He was banged up in the playoffs, but through the 11 games he played, he averaged 15.1 points. That made him the Thunder's second-leading scorer.

Looking into next season, Mitchell's role should change as one of the Thunder's most important pieces off the bench. He has a legitimate shot at winning sixth man of the year, with the second-best odds , according to FanDuel, just behind Dylan Harper.

A great candidate for a leap is fourth-year forward Brandon Miller. The former No. 2 pick has quietly put together three strong seasons despite playing only 27 games in his second season.

For Miller' s career, he's averaged 19 points while shooting 37.3 percent from three. He's coming off a career-high 38.3 percent from three on 8.2 attempts. He was a member of the three-headed monster with LaMelo Ball and Kon Knueppel that made the Hornets the surprise story of the season.

This season, Miller will have more opportunities to show off his playmaking skills. He will play without Ball and Miles Bridges after already having a high usage rate of 27.2 percent . Expect the ball to be in Miller's hands more, and he can show another facet of his game that has not been shown too often.

The Hornets made a big bet trading Ball, one of those bets is that Miller alongside Kon Knueppel will flourish with more opportunities to have the ball in their hands. Miller is the favorite on FanDuel for the Most Improved Player award.

2025-26 was a lost season for Walker Kessler, who played only five games for the Utah Jazz. But after a sign-and-trade that has him as a Los Angeles Laker, Kessler has a chance to take a major leap forward.

Kessler has not been a beacon of good health throughout his career; his games-played total has dropped each consecutive season. However, when he is on the floor, he's been a good rebounder, averaging 12.2 rebounds during the 2024-25 season, along with 2.4 blocks.

What makes this season a leap opportunity for Kessler is that he gets to play with one of the best lob-throwers in the NBA, Luka Doncic. Getting that opportunity to catch lobs and also rebound the misses from Doncic as he rolls to the rim should see his scoring numbers go up. Kessler is a great pick-and-roll partner for Luka, and it should pay immediate dividends.

In the few games Kessler played last season, he experimented with adding a three-ball, attempting 1.6 three-pointers over five games. If that is an addition to his game, that would be a pretty big leap and would be worth the hefty price the Lakers paid for him.

Scoot Henderson missed most of the 2025-26 season but played in the Portland Trail Blazers' last 29 games. Health has held back his development for multiple seasons. However, last season showed all the flashes that made him the third pick in the 2023 draft.

The biggest market against Henderson has been his shooting, but in the last 21 games , he shot 40.1 percent on five attempts. That continued in the playoffs, where he shot 46.4 percent in their five-game first-round series against the San Antonio Spurs. That includes a 31-point explosion in Game 2 of the series—the only game the Blazers won.

On top of the stretch of shooting from Henderson, he was one of the better defenders for the Blazers. While he was on the floor, Portland had a defensive rating of 109; that is 4.8 points better than when he was off the floor.

If there is one possible obstacle to Henderson taking a leap this coming season, it might be the depth chart. The Blazers will get Damian Lillard back this season, just acquired Ja Morant and still have Jrue Holiday on the roster. That is a very crowded backcourt that might make it difficult for Henderson to see the court enough to actually take the leap.

Mo Dakhil spent six years with the Los Angeles Clippers and two years with the San Antonio Spurs as a video coordinator, as well as three years with the Australian men's national team. Follow him on X, @MoDakhil_NBA .
